tools.name: vallum_doctor
tools.description: Inspect platform readiness, Linux capabilities, helper tools (ip, systemctl, journalctl, resolvconf, nft), and control socket health. Returns a structured JSON report.

outputs.description: Array of system readiness checks with status ('pass', 'warn', 'fail') and diagnostic detail.

tools.name: vallum_doctor_config
tools.description: Perform a comprehensive health check on a specific Vallum configuration file and its declared control socket. Returns a structured JSON report.

config_path.description: Path to the .toml configuration file to validate.

tools.name: vallum_show_config
tools.description: Inspect a Vallum configuration and its peer definitions offline without requiring a running daemon. Returns structured JSON containing interface settings, addresses, listen port, and peers.

config_path.description: Path to the .toml configuration file to inspect.

tools.name: vallum_show_control
tools.description: Query a live running Vallum daemon via its UNIX control socket. Returns real-time interface metrics, active peers, latest handshake timestamps, and transfer bytes in JSON.

control_socket.description: Path to the UNIX domain control socket (e.g., /run/vallum/vallum0.sock).

tools.name: vallum_keygen
tools.description: Generate a post-quantum hybrid private key file (with strict 0600 permissions) and output the public line for peers. Defaults to tri-hybrid Suite 3 (X25519 + sntrup761 + ML-KEM-768).

output_file.description: File path where the private key will be saved.

suite.description: Crypto suite ID (default 3 for tri-hybrid PQ).

tools.name: vallum_pubkey
tools.description: Extract and compute the public line from an existing private key file.

private_key_file.description: Path to the private key file.

tools.name: vallum_genpsk
tools.description: Generate a 32-byte (64 hex characters) preshared key (PSK) to provide symmetric post-quantum defense against Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later.

outputs.description: 64 hex characters representing the 32-byte preshared key.

tools.name: vallum_bench
tools.description: Benchmark the post-quantum data plane seal/open cryptographic performance on the current host. Both arguments are required because a CLI template substitutes them into the command verbatim: pass 2000 and 1380 for the defaults.

iterations.description: Number of iterations to benchmark (the CLI default is 2000).

bytes.description: Payload size in bytes (the CLI default is 1380).

tools.name: vallum_syncconf
tools.description: Apply only the differences between a configuration file and a running Vallum daemon without terminating existing sessions.

config_path.description: Path to the configuration file containing updated peer or interface settings.

tools.name: vallum_tui_snapshot
tools.description: Render a single headless frame of the Vallum TUI dashboard or status views. Bypasses TTY requirements so agents and CI harnesses can inspect visual dashboard state without hanging or crashing. All three arguments are required because a CLI template substitutes them verbatim: pass dashboard, 120 and 36 for the defaults.

outputs.description: ASCII / text frame render of the TUI view.

tools.name: vallum_status
tools.description: Answer "is traffic in the tunnel, blocked, or leaking?" by reading the host rather than the process, so it still works when the daemon is dead. Verdicts: up, degraded, stale, starting, blocked, down, LEAKING, unknown. `stale` means the daemon answers but its last handshake is past the 180 s reject window, so the session is dead while the process lives. Only LEAKING exits non-zero.

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config.

tools.name: vallum_policy
tools.description: Install, remove, or report the fail-closed egress block. `on` blocks everything except loopback, the tunnel and the peer endpoint; `off` removes it and needs neither daemon nor network; `status` reports what the config asks for and what the host has, in one object: `declared` (what the config says), `policy` (`declared` with `auto` resolved), `guard` (installed/absent/unknown), `egress` (blocked/unrestricted/unknown) and `fix` when a guard is wanted but missing. Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN for `on` and `off`.

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config.

tools.name: vallum_metrics
tools.description: Print the daemon's state as Prometheus metrics: per-peer bytes, handshake age, epoch, and vallum_peer_delivery_ratio — datagrams received over datagrams sent in the last 60 s window. A ratio near zero means the tunnel is sending and not being answered, which handshake age cannot show. An idle peer reports 1. Shell-only flags this template cannot express: `--control` (a socket instead of a config), `--prefix`, and `--output` (an atomic write for a `node_exporter` textfile collector — the file still gets `up 0` when the daemon is silent, while the command exits nonzero).

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config.

tools.name: vallum_peer_list
tools.description: List peers with their allowed prefixes, endpoint, keepalive, and fingerprint. Use the fingerprint to map a peer to the label in vallum_metrics.

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config.

tools.name: vallum_peer_show
tools.description: Read one peer: prefixes, endpoint, keepalive, PSK, endpoint pinning, identity validity and fingerprint. This is the read before `vallum_peer_remove`, which has no dry run.

name.description: The peer's name in the config.

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config.

tools.name: vallum_peer_add
tools.description: Enrol a device that generated its own key: writes the peer into the server's config, allocates one address per family the interface carries, and tells a running daemon. The fingerprint it returns is the label vallum_metrics uses. Shell-only flags this template cannot express: `--bundle-out`/`--ship-key` (the server generating a client's key — a server compromise then means a client compromise), `--dns` (repeatable), `--psk`, `--pin-endpoint`, `--allowed-ips`, `--address`, `--keepalive`, `--shaping`, `--no-apply`.

name.description: The name this device will have on the server.

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config.

public_key.description: The device's own public line (`vallum1:0003:…`), printed by `vallum pubkey` on the device.

tools.name: vallum_peer_invite
tools.description: Mint a single-use enrolment ticket so a device can join without SSH. The returned `ticket` is what the device runs: `vallum join <ticket>`. It expires after `ttl_minutes` and works once. The `token` is a secret — pass it to the device, never into a log or a transcript.

name.description: The name the device will enrol under.

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config.

ttl_minutes.description: How long the invite lives, in minutes.

commands.command: vallum peer invite UTCP_ARG_name_UTCP_END --config UTCP_ARG_config_UTCP_END --ttl UTCP_ARG_ttl_minutes_UTCP_END --json

tools.name: vallum_peer_invites
tools.description: List live one-time invites with their remaining TTL, pruning expired ones. Tokens are never printed here, so this is the safe half of inviting: use it to check whether the ticket you handed out was spent.

config.description: Path to the server's TOML config.

tools.name: vallum_peer_remove
tools.description: Remove a peer from the config and tell a running daemon. Immediate: there is no dry run, so call `vallum_peer_show` first and keep the reported `backup` path — it is the only undo. Removing a peer does not revoke its key; rotate the server's identity if the device was lost.

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config.

tools.name: vallum_server_init_plan
tools.description: Print every host change `vallum server init` would make (key, config, units, firewall, forwarding, NAT) without changing anything. Call this first: the apply tool below starts a root daemon, opens a UDP port and edits forwarding. Needs no root.

config.description: Path to the .toml config that would be written.

outputs.description: The plan, one step per line, each prefixed `would`.

tools.name: vallum_server_init
tools.description: Provision this host as a server: generate keys, write the config, install and start the systemd units, open the listen port, and enable forwarding and masquerade. Handles a UFW deny (routed) default. Needs root. Run `vallum_server_init_plan` first — that is the console's plan-then-apply rule, and this tool is the apply. One address per family is chosen for you (10.7.0.1/24, fd00:7::1/64); anything else needs `vallum server init --address` (repeatable) from a shell, and `--force` to rewrite an existing config is likewise not exposed here.

config.description: Path to the .toml config to write.

outputs.description: The provisioning report with --json: config, key, interface, addresses, listen, endpoint, public_key, firewall, host_steps[], service, control, and next — the one command to run next.

tools.name: vallum_server_teardown_plan
tools.description: Print what `vallum_server_teardown` would remove — units, NAT, firewall rules, the forwarding sysctl — without changing the host. The counterpart of `vallum_server_init_plan`; call it before the teardown so a trial server can be reversed on evidence rather than on faith. Needs no root.

config.description: Path to the server config being torn down.

outputs.description: The plan, one step per line, each prefixed `would`.

tools.name: vallum_server_teardown
tools.description: Reverse `vallum_server_init`: stop and disable the units, remove the NAT table, firewall accepts and the forwarding sysctl. Needs root. The config and its key are kept, so `vallum_server_init` can bring the same server back; `--purge` deletes them too and is not exposed here.

config.description: Path to the server config being torn down.

outputs.description: One line per removed step, then `torn down: server <name>`.

tools.name: vallum_join
tools.description: Enrol this machine as a client with the one-time `vallum1-join:…` ticket `vallum peer invite` printed on the server. The ticket carries the responder address, invite id, token and the server fingerprint in one string, so there are no other flags to get right. On a root host this writes /etc/vallum and starts the tunnel; `vallum_join_plan` prints the same steps without changing anything. Fails if the invite expired, was minted for another name, or the server is unreachable.

outputs.description: The config written, the key, and the unit started.

tools.name: vallum_join_plan
tools.description: Print what `vallum_join` would write and start for a ticket, without contacting the server or changing the host. Use it when the ticket is in hand and the intent is not yet certain.

outputs.description: The plan, one step per line.

tools.name: vallum_import_bundle
tools.description: Install this machine as a client from the `.vallum-bundle` file a server wrote: /etc/vallum, the key at 0600, the units, and the tunnel started. Needs root. A bundle that carries `[quick]` hooks — strings that run as root — is refused unless `--allow-hooks` is passed, which this tool does not do: a hook-bearing bundle must be read by a person first.

outputs.description: The config path, the key path at 0600, and the unit started.

tools.name: vallum_stop
tools.description: Ask a running daemon to stop and wait for its acknowledgement, so a script that calls this can trust the tunnel is down afterwards. Reads the control socket from the config.

config.description: Path to the tunnel's TOML config, for its `control` path.

outputs.description: The daemon's acknowledgement, or an error if it did not answer.
